title: Forward attention, nine A2/A3 sources
formula: out = softmax(mask(Q @ K^T / sqrt(D))) @ V over head-major [rows, D] tensors, D 128 or 256, FP16 or BF16 in, FP32 or BF16 out, probabilities stored in FP16, BF16 or HiFloat8; pv_stage instead publishes the unnormalized exp(score - rowmax) @ V of each 128-key tile
study_for: Nine sources that differ in ABI, not only in schedule -- and MODELS in reference.py is what lets one reference formula serve all nine. Each entry names the key-group size the online softmax rescales at, the precision the probabilities are stored in before PV, whether the mask is causal, and whether the variant publishes normalized attention or unnormalized partial PV. Read MODELS before reading any kernel body: it is the shortest statement of what each variant actually computes.

`pv_stage` is in this family and is not attention. It publishes S2 // 128 unnormalized partial PV results per query row and never divides by a denominator, which is why its comparison carries atol 2e-2 -- the numbers have not been scaled back down by a softmax denominator, so an absolute bound on them is not the same quantity as an absolute bound on an attention output. Copying its tolerance onto a normalized kernel would be a much weaker check than it looks.

Why the elementwise bounds are loose and the relative L2 is the real gate. The probabilities are stored at the source's own precision, so one that lands near a rounding midpoint of that format goes to opposite neighbours under two independent exp() implementations. A single straddle is derived to cost up to 1.5e-02 at D=256 while moving the relative L2 by about 2e-05, so no pointwise bound can be promised and the residual is what actually rejects missing work. The wider rtol on the BF16-output variants is load-bearing, not slack to reclaim.

What had to be renamed when nine modules became one file, and why each rename is a real difference rather than a merge artefact. Two entirely different kernels were both called `flash_attn_full_pj_hif8_kernel` and are now `flash_attn_full_pj_hif8_bf16_lag2_kernel` and `flash_attn_full_pj_hif8_fp16_lag1_kernel`. Three different (lookahead, slots) rings shared the names GROUP_LOOKAHEAD/GROUP_STAGE_SLOTS and are now DENSE_ (2/4), RING_ (3/5) and D256_ (2/4). Most dangerous of all, `HALF_M = TILE_M // 2` is the same line of text in every module but a different number in the D=256 pair, whose M tile is 64 rows -- so the d256 family carries D256_TILE_M and D256_HALF_M and a d256_ prefix on every masking helper that reads them.

`is_causal` on the d256 pair is a run-time kernel argument, not a build-time variant: the same emitted kernel serves `full_*` and `block32_*` cases, and the eight case pairs in main.py differ only in that one scalar. That is the cheapest available control for a mask -- same schedule, same tiling, same inputs, one switch.
do_not_copy_when: You want one attention kernel to read. This is nine of them plus a partial stage; pick the variant that matches your dtype and ABI and read only that one, or read a5_mha_fp16_bf16 for a single algorithm with three schedules instead.

You need a head dimension other than 128 or 256. The two widths are separate sources here with separate tile geometry -- the D=256 pair halves the M tile to 64 rows to pay for it -- and neither generalizes to a third width by changing a constant.

You want GQA or MQA without reading gqa_bf16 specifically. It is the only one of the nine whose K and V carry a different head count from Q; everything else in this folder assumes one KV head per query head, and a shared-KV layout changes the head mapping, the L1 residency and the partition together.

You are copying a tolerance. Every variant declares its own, for a numerical reason stated in main.py; the family-wide strictest rule is not safe for a BF16 output and the pv_stage rule is not safe for anything normalized.
